candidates: In `gitGraphRenderer.js`, when adding or modifying a vertical graph orientation, always derive a commit's rendered position from its closest parent's stored position (`commitPos[closestParent]`) rather than from the current commit's own pre-computed `commitPos[key]`; orientations that share the same axis (e.g., `TB` and `BT`) should be collapsed into a single `dir === 'TB' || dir === 'BT'` branch to keep position-calculation logic consistent and avoid subtle divergence bugs.

Do not introduce magic numbers (raw numeric literals) as layout or geometry constants in renderer code; extract every such value into a named variable or constant (e.g., `const commitStep = 40`, `const layoutOffset = 10`) so that the intent is clear and the value is easy to change consistently.

Never rename or otherwise modify the title strings of existing test cases in snapshot-based or image-comparison test suites (such as the Cypress `imgSnapshotTest` suite); test titles are used to derive snapshot file names, so renaming an existing title causes all prior baseline images for that test to be orphaned and the comparison to fail.

When adding new test cases that cover a new variant of an existing feature (e.g., a new graph orientation), group them in a new nested `describe` block rather than appending to or altering the names of existing test cases; this keeps the snapshot namespace stable and makes the test hierarchy self-documenting.

New feature sections in Mermaid documentation must include `(v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)` as a version placeholder in the section heading (e.g., `### Bottom to Top (\`BT:\`) (v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)`); never hardcode a specific version string, as the placeholder is replaced automatically during the release pipeline.
